selected_result: Theorem 3.2: probabilistic backward error for subtracting an inner product and dividing

bibliographic_source.title: A New Approach to Probabilistic Rounding Error Analysis

paper_locations.anchor: Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.7), with the Model 2.1 and gamma-tilde definitions on PDF pages 4-6

task_clarification: Let k be positive, b_k nonzero, and y=(c-sum_{i=1}^{k-1} a_i*b_i)/b_k. The source evaluates this subtraction-inner-product-division kernel in floating-point arithmetic, with any legal order of evaluation.

Use the paper's standard relative-error operation rule and Model 2.1: every operation error is independent, mean zero, and bounded in absolute value by the unit roundoff u. This is an assumption about the random execution, not a claim about ordinary deterministic rounding.

For every lambda>0, with probability at least Q(lambda,k), there must exist perturbations mu_0,...,mu_{k-1} satisfying yhat*b_k*(1+mu_0)=c-sum_{i=1}^{k-1} a_i*b_i*(1+mu_i), and every |mu_i|<=gammaTilde_k(lambda).
gammaTilde and Q are exactly the source's equations (2.1), (2.2), and (3.1). The perturbations must be witnesses inside the high-probability event.
scope_constraints: Quantify over all allowed evaluation orders; a proof for only one convenient parenthesization does not cover the theorem.
Do not assume the desired backward equation, perturbation witnesses, probability event, or final bound as fields of the execution model.
Preserve the nonzero divisor, all source parameters, and the exact Q(lambda,k) and gammaTilde_k(lambda) factors.
